parsed.why: No trans criminalisation, but tier-3 hostility with thin recourse: documented trans killings, refused service and space exclusion, birth-sex jail housing with head-shaving, police arrests of Pride participants, local cross-dressing bans. National protections stalled; remedies fragmented.

No visitor-facing restrictions documented; supportive law and long reform trajectory, self-declared markers, conversion ban. Deduction for documented rising hate incidents (229, up 42%) and survey showing one in five threatened, 8% physically attacked.

No trans offence and a third-gender tradition, but frequent physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans people in public and government settings, conversion practices, and newly rising anti-LGBTQ political hostility; marker changes remain discretionary.

Colonial sodomy felonies (14/7/5 years) reach trans women read as male, with no gender-identity protection and no enforcement record since 2013; offset only by a third-gender tradition and no documented anti-trans abuse.

Gender presentation itself criminalised (Article 152) alongside sodomy (up to five years, life for a third offence), no recognition, blocked transition care, and documented state extrajudicial killings, torture and official discrimination.
